incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are stealing his identity to defraud vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal offering immigration services he never provides, such as US residency assistance for $2,200. The scheme escalated dramatically in recent months, with scammers directing victims through social media to contact phone numbers via WhatsApp, where they exchange fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle.

After potential clients began calling his office about these fraudulent services, Leal hired an online anti-piracy company to combat the fraud. The company has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. He warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to be suspicious of requests for immediate payment through digital payment apps.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake article featuring Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated confrontation with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler is among a growing wave of AI-generated investment scams. The fabricated interview promoted Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The scam never actually occurred, but such deceptive tactics are becoming increasingly common and sophisticated. ASIC reports that AI-powered schemes using deepfake images or videos of celebrities and politicians are rising rapidly. Last year, the regulator removed 19,400 scams total, representing a 182 percent increase from the previous year, with phishing scams jumping 279 percent and fake investment platforms increasing 151 percent.

Scammers typically build elaborate webs of deception using fake brands, news articles, positive reviews, and advertisements to lure victims. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is the most commonly impersonated public figure, followed by politicians and prominent financial experts including Kohler himself. ASIC advises consumers to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers through official registers before investing. Presenter Kohler argues that penalties for platforms hosting such content and the AI models creating it should be stricter.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Oura, the smart ring manufacturer, by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco. The suit alleges that the company engaged in false advertising by claiming its rings can accurately track sleep stages with 95% accuracy comparable to clinical sleep laboratories, when the devices allegedly cannot reliably measure the physiological signals needed for such precision. The lawsuit contends that Oura's algorithms and sensors produce results no better than random guesses, while the company markets rings priced at $300 and up based on their supposed sleep tracking capabilities.

Oura responded by defending its science and accuracy claims, stating that its devices use multiple physiological signals including heart rate and temperature to estimate sleep stages and have been validated in peer-reviewed studies. The company emphasized that its rings are not medical devices and should not be substituted for clinical sleep studies. A CNET expert noted that health trackers provide estimates rather than definitive measurements and that consumers should not overemphasize single data points. The lawsuit seeks class-action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear what compensation affected customers could receive if the case proceeds.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual environments. The group operated across multiple countries and ran a data leak site. Researchers found that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The ESXi ransomware variant uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes specific features to shut down virtual machines and encrypt their files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see the ransom demand.

The investigation also identified a second Aurora cluster with medium confidence attribution, targeting eight organizations across Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This cluster used different tactics including SQL Server vulnerabilities and S3 bucket exfiltration. Researchers provided technical details about the ransomware's command-line options, custom scanning tools for finding ESXi hosts, and multiple indicators of compromise including IP addresses, URLs, and file hashes to help organizations detect and defend against these attacks.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas in May alleging that the chain's mandatory adoption of Dragontail, an artificial intelligence-powered delivery management system, caused significant operational problems and $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, claims the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately. The franchisee says this resulted in late deliveries and poor customer satisfaction, while delivery performance dropped from over 90 percent on-time arrivals to significantly worse metrics after the 2024 rollout.

The lawsuit argues that Pizza Hut breached its franchise agreement by mandating the software without adequate training or support and failing to modify the system to work with Chaac's business model. The franchisee points to sharp sales declines in major markets, including New York City where annual growth shifted from positive 10.19 percent to negative 9.78 percent. Pizza Hut stated it was reviewing the claims and would respond through legal channels. The lawsuit comes as Pizza Hut's parent company has struggled with declining sales and announced plans to close 250 US locations this year.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
Scammers are sending fraudulent emails impersonating Terry Gross and other staff members from WHYY's "Fresh Air" radio program to solicit money from authors, entertainers and other public figures. The highly personalized messages reference the recipient's work and propose interview topics, creating the appearance of a legitimate booking process. Recipients are eventually asked to pay fees for production costs, with some emails originating from fake addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com. WHYY, NPR and law enforcement are investigating the scheme, which has affected numerous targets including academics and comedians.

According to cybersecurity experts, artificial intelligence has made these traditional impersonation scams more convincing and personalized than ever before. Red flags include requests for payment, emails claiming to be from Gross herself rather than production staff, and suspicious gmail addresses. WHYY has clarified that it never charges guests for interviews and does not pay people to appear on the show. Experts recommend verifying any interview invitation by contacting the organization directly through legitimate channels rather than responding to the suspicious email.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake American research organization called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to optimize content for artificial intelligence chatbots. The organization, which does not exist as a legal entity and has no staff or physical address, presented pro-Israel arguments on contentious topics including Palestinian torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation as neutral research. A New York media company called Piro Inc filed the site with the US Justice Department as material distributed for the Israeli government under foreign agent disclosure requirements.

The operation represents part of a broader campaign funded by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government, routed through the European advertising group Havas Media, to influence how AI systems frame Israel-related issues. Researchers found the reports used problematic sourcing practices, repeatedly citing one 2022 study about antisemitic Facebook comments across dozens of unrelated articles and applying caveats that obscured facts. Israeli officials have expressed frustration about such public diplomacy efforts, with one stating the government paid substantial money but the situation worsened. Recent polling shows American support for Israel has declined significantly, with Palestinians gaining more sympathy than Israelis for the first time in February.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed separate lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno, accusing them of copying thousands of copyrighted songs without permission. The labels allege that the companies scraped massive amounts of music to train their AI models and that the generators can directly reproduce sections of famous songs. The lawsuits include a list of thousands of copyrighted works allegedly used in training, featuring artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Michael Jackson, and Coldplay. The record labels claim that when they tested the platforms with specific prompts, they successfully recreated versions of copyrighted songs, demonstrating that the originals were likely part of the training data.

The record labels submitted their lawsuits in New York against Udio and Massachusetts against Suno, where Suno is headquartered. Court documents include audio examples showing AI-generated outputs that closely resemble famous songs, such as a Suno creation copying Chuck Berry's style and a near-identical reproduction of Mariah Carey's holiday song. The companies have previously claimed their training on copyrighted material constitutes fair use, but have refused to disclose which songs they trained on. This legal action represents a major battle over how generative AI services should operate and whether they can legally use existing creative works for training purposes.

# Summary

Universal Music Group has settled its lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, reaching licensing agreements to resolve disputes over copyrighted music used to train the company's artificial intelligence system. Udio creates original songs from text prompts and had been accused of using hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" to generate similar compositions without permission. Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year trained only on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize and share compositions while compensating artists who opt in.

The collaboration marks Udio's first major label licensing deal and reflects broader efforts to reconcile AI innovation with music industry protections. UMG's CEO stated the agreement demonstrates the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technologies. Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am, has attracted millions of users since its launch. The company declined to disclose specific financial terms or compensation details for participating artists.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's lawyers apologized after they used artificial intelligence to draft legal motions that contained fabricated case citations, fake quotes, and nonexistent legal holdings in a lawsuit filed by a Los Angeles homeowner. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire destroyed her Carson home. She claimed that delays in getting State Farm's approval for storm damage repairs prevented the reconstruction from being completed, forcing her family to declare bankruptcy and lose their home to foreclosure. The case is scheduled for trial in October.

Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted that seven case citations across eight court filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and misquoted material. She had used an AI tool called Irys, believing it would catch errors, but it did not. The incident highlights a growing problem in the legal profession, where 41 percent of law firms now use generative AI. A Paris-based researcher has documented nearly 1,900 cases of AI-generated legal hallucinations worldwide, with most occurring in the United States.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Summary:
An investment analyst recommends three artificial intelligence stocks as particularly attractive purchases in September, despite the month's historical tendency to underperform. Nvidia, Amazon, and Micron Technology are highlighted as top opportunities for investors. Nvidia recently reported exceptional second-quarter earnings with revenue growth of 106% year-over-year and expects 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, demonstrating continued strong demand for its graphics processing units despite investor concerns about future GPU demand.

Micron manufactures memory chips currently experiencing significant supply shortages due to high demand from artificial intelligence development, allowing the company to raise prices and boost profits while it constructs new production facilities expected to come online in 2027 and 2028. Amazon, though not typically associated with artificial intelligence investing, is aggressively investing in its cloud computing division with $220 billion in capital expenditures this year, and the resulting growth in Amazon Web Services is accelerating at 37% year-over-year, increasingly driving the company's overall profitability.

stories.Headline: 《TAIPEI TIMES》 Taiwan aims to train 500,000 AI pros by 2040 - 焦點
stories.Summary:
Taiwan's government plans to invest over 40 billion Taiwan dollars, approximately 1.26 billion US dollars, to develop 10 major artificial intelligence projects next year. President William Lai has set an ambitious goal to train at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. The administration launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development, and data-driven approaches, aiming to build a large AI talent pool and strengthen Taiwan's competitiveness in technology sectors.

The government is also prioritizing technological sovereignty and national resilience. The Minister of Digital Affairs announced plans to accumulate at least 10,000 graphics processing units through private investment in AI computing centers within a year. Taiwan is focusing on developing sovereign AI systems that understand Taiwanese perspectives and languages, along with low-Earth-orbit satellite communications to ensure independent communication capabilities. Officials emphasized that technological sovereignty means focusing on critical technologies rather than developing every technology domestically.

stories.Headline: CSA's Top Cloud Threats: Identity, AI -- Campus Technology
stories.Summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance surveyed 507 security professionals to identify the top threats to cloud computing in 2026. Identity and access management issues rose to the number one concern, moving up from second place in 2024, while misconfiguration dropped to fifth. Two artificial intelligence-related threats appeared in the rankings for the first time, including AI-enhanced attacks and AI system compromise. The top eleven threats also include insecure third-party resources, insecure APIs, advanced persistent threats, and inadequate cloud security strategy and governance.

The survey results reveal a significant shift in the cloud threat landscape, with organizations now prioritizing identity protection, artificial intelligence risks, and software supply chains over infrastructure-focused concerns. Security scores ranged closely from 7.95 for identity and access management to 7.45 for system vulnerabilities. The report aims to help organizations make informed risk-management decisions about cloud adoption by providing expert analysis of technical and business impacts, real-world examples, and corresponding security controls across cloud and AI environments.

stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their partnership in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. During a meeting at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi, president of Saudi Arabia's Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority, discussed ways to establish a comprehensive and sustainable cooperation between the two nations.

Khawaja presented Pakistan's current initiatives to advance its national artificial intelligence and data governance agenda, while emphasizing the country's dedication to building a robust data ecosystem and strengthening its digital economy. The officials agreed to continue their discussions to further strengthen the partnership in these technology areas.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: Environmental News Network - AI Project Led by UH Aims to Protect Hawaiʻi's Coastal Freshwater
stories.Summary:
The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa is launching an artificial intelligence project to forecast threats to coastal freshwater supplies and ecosystems. Associate Professor Jonghyun Lee received a $500,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to lead the initiative, which is part of a broader three-year collaborative effort worth nearly $1 million involving the University of Texas at Austin. The project aims to develop AI applications in geoscience to better understand environmental challenges.

Rising ocean levels, intensified storms, saltwater infiltration of freshwater sources, and coastal ecosystem damage present growing dangers to communities throughout the region. These threats directly endanger drinking water availability, farming operations, infrastructure, and the economic wellbeing of millions of people who depend on coastal areas.

India is hosting its first dedicated summit focused on artificial intelligence in marketing in September 2026. The AIM Summit will take place on September 17 in Bengaluru and September 18 in New Delhi, bringing together over 50 chief marketing officers from major brands including Paytm, KFC, Nestle, and Uniqlo. The event expects to attract more than 600 marketing professionals as attendees and delegates.

The summit aims to move beyond theoretical discussions about artificial intelligence and instead focus on practical implementation and real-world applications. The program will include an AI Lab for hands-on exploration of technology capabilities, an exhibition showcasing marketing solution providers, and an awards ceremony recognizing innovative organizations. Sessions will cover topics such as content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation, and analytics. The summit is being organized with CXO Lanes, a community of over 500,000 executives across India.

stories.Headline: Dyna.Ai Selected as Technology Partner in Hong Kong's GenA.I. Sandbox++
stories.Summary:
Dyna.Ai, a Singapore-based AI company, has been selected as a technology partner in Hong Kong's new GenA.I. Sandbox++ program, marking its second consecutive selection by Hong Kong financial regulators. The sandbox was jointly launched by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Securities and Futures Commission, Insurance Authority, and Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority in collaboration with Cyberport. Out of nearly 100 regional proposals, 36 use cases involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology providers were chosen, including major institutions like Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Manulife (International), alongside technology partners Google, IBM, and Dyna.Ai.

Unlike earlier programs focused on generative AI banking pilots, Sandbox++ expands across banking, insurance, securities, and pension funds to test Agentic AI systems that execute complex tasks under real-time governance. Dyna.Ai will demonstrate how financial institutions can safely delegate workflow execution to autonomous AI agents while maintaining strict oversight and compliance. The company plans to showcase its solutions and governance frameworks at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh later this year.
